name: Compose
grades: A: no errors and at most 1 warning. B: no errors. C: 1 error. D: 2 errors. F: 3 or more. Each rule counts once, however many places it fires. Hints never count.

1.name: The thing being made fills the middle

2.name: A way out (Cancel, Close, X, back or Exit)

4.name: Tool strip or row of tool tabs

v1.name: Text composer
expect: The text page fills the middle of the screen
A way out, Cancel or Close, sits at the top
A commit button such as Post, Done or Next
The keyboard is open along the bottom

v2.name: Photo or video editor
expect: The picture or clip fills the middle of the screen
A commit button such as Done, Next or Send
A way out, Cancel or Close, next to it

v3.name: Canvas or builder
expect: The board, page or timeline fills the middle of the screen
A tool strip or row of tool tabs
A way out at the top of the screen

not_checked: What happens after the tap on the commit button, and whether the work is saved or thrown away: one screen cannot show it.
Whether undo, redo and the tools change the work, and how the work looks in a second state.
Whether the keyboard comes up by itself when a text page opens.

rules.says: Text breaks in the middle of a word.
rules.why: Text breaks in the middle of a word on the card ('Christma' then 's!') because of wide letter spacing. Seen on 1 of 52 checked screens.

rules.says: Tool labels are small and pale against their background.
rules.why: Tool labels are very small and pale grey. Seen on 3 of 52 checked screens.

rules.says: Labels on the canvas or timeline are too small to read.
rules.why: Labels on the timeline are too small to read. Seen on 2 of 52 checked screens.

rules.says: The thing being made is not on the screen.

rules.why: Only 2 of 10 Photo or video editor screens have it, so position/6 does not apply to a screen of this variant.

rules.says: Text or a close control is too faint against what is behind it.
rules.why: Accessibility guidelines ask for 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text: 18 pt, or 14 pt bold (button labels are bold). Controls, such as a close or back glyph, need 3:1. Below 3:1 is an error; from 3:1 to 4.5:1 on smaller text it is a warning. Checked on the labels of buttons, the lines of the parts marked as key text, and the close and back glyphs. Not checked on a dimmed screen or over a photo or a pattern.

rules.says: Text is smaller than 11 pt.
rules.why: Apple lists 11 pt as the smallest text size on iOS. Measured from the height of each line, so it is about right, not exact. Checked on the parts marked as key text.

rules.says: A control sits under the status bar or the home indicator.
rules.why: The status bar row at the top and the bottom 34 pt, where the home indicator sits, belong to the system on phones without a home button. Flagged when a control reaches the status bar row or comes within 17 pt of the bottom edge, so a button that only touches the area is not counted.

rules.says: A close or back control is drawn smaller than 13 pt.
rules.why: Apple asks for a 44 x 44 pt tap area. The standard close X in a bar is drawn about 13 to 17 pt across inside that area, so only a smaller drawing is flagged. A screenshot cannot show the tap area itself, so this is a hint.
